query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Minor Mo additions to the CoCrFeNi base alloy will promote the formation of stable, high-temperature tribo-oxides that protect the sliding interface from room temperature up to 800 °C, thus reducing friction and wear compared to the undoped alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: A standard CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix prepared via vacuum or arc melting, solution-annealed, and homogenized.
generation.intervention: Alloying CoCrFeNi with a small amount of Mo (e.g., 2–5 at.%) during the melting and casting process to facilitate in situ tribofilm formation.
generation.conditions: Dry sliding tests from 25 °C to 800 °C in mildly oxidative atmospheres, using standard pin-on-disk or ball-on-disk tribometers under a normal load (e.g., 5–10 N) and sliding speeds of ~0.1–0.5 m/s.
generation.structural_mediator: Mo-induced tribo-oxide scale at high temperatures.
generation.mechanism: Mo modifies near-surface compositional and oxide chemistry, forming stable oxygen-rich protective films that reduce direct metal–metal contact and deter abrasive/adhesive wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to undoped CoCrFeNi, the Mo-doped alloy will maintain a lower and more stable coefficient of friction (COF < 0.4) and reduced wear rate (on the order of 10^-5 mm³/N·m or lower) continuously from room temperature through 800 °C.
generation.baseline: Undoped CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy of the same processing route tested in identical tribological conditions.
generation.boundary: Benefits are expected under dry sliding or mildly oxidative conditions, using moderate loads (5–10 N) and up to 800 °C. Significant changes to environment (e.g., corrosive media) or extreme load/velocity regimes may require additional optimization.
generation.uncertainty: While prior studies on Mo additions to other high-entropy alloys suggest improved tribological stability, the ideal Mo content and any synergy with other microalloying elements remain to be confirmed specifically for CoCrFeNi.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of specimens: (1) baseline CoCrFeNi and (2) CoCrFeNi + 2–5 at.% Mo. Subject both sets to identical tribological tests from 25 °C to 800 °C in air using the same load, speed, track, and environment. Measure friction coefficient, wear volume, and analyze worn surfaces via SEM/EDS to confirm the presence of Mo-based oxides.
measurements: Coefficient of friction as a function of temperature
Quantification of wear volume and wear rates
Surface morphology and oxide identification by SEM/EDS or XRD
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the incorporation of Mo does not lead to a statistically significant decrease in friction and wear rates across the entire 25–800 °C range relative to the baseline, or if no stabilizing tribo-oxide layer is observed, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractAlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy (HEA) films with strong amorphization were obtained by co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition, and the effect of thermal shock on the films was investigated in order to explore the protection mechanism of HEA films against mechanical components in extreme service environments. The results show that after annealing at 800 °C for 1 h, the formation of a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on the surface actively prevents the oxidation from continuing, so that the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film exhibits excellent oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air. In the friction-corrosion coupling environment, the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film annealed at 800 °C for 1 h shows the best tribocorrosion resistance due to the stable dense microstructure and excellent mechanical properties, and its ΔOCP, COF and wear rate possess the smallest values of 0.055, 0.04 and 1.34 × 10−6 mm−3·N−1·m−1.Keywords: AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film, thermal shock, oxidation, tribocorrosion
